title: Split square-zero flat deformations of algebraic spaces and cotangent Ext
statement:
Let $K$ be any field [def-weil-field], let $X$ be an algebraic space over $\operatorname{Spec}K$ [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-weil-affine-spectrum], and suppose $X\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ is flat, meaning flat on etale scheme charts [def-weil-flat-morphism]. For a $K$-vector space $M$, put $K\oplus M=K\times M$ with $(a,m)(b,n)=(ab,an+bm)$, and $Y_M=\operatorname{Spec}(K\oplus M)$. Let $\operatorname{Def}_X(M)$ be the set of isomorphism classes of flat algebraic spaces $X'\to Y_M$ equipped with an identification $X'\times_{Y_M}\operatorname{Spec}K\cong X$; isomorphisms must respect that identification. Let $\operatorname{Aut}^0_X(M)$ be the group of automorphisms of the trivial family $X\times_KY_M$ over $Y_M$ inducing the identity on $X$. With $\mathrm{NL}$ and Ext as in [def-sfb-space-naive-cotangent-complex], there are natural identifications
$$\operatorname{Def}_X(M)\cong\operatorname{Ext}^1_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathrm{NL}_{X/K},\mathcal O_X\otimes_K M),\qquad \operatorname{Aut}^0_X(M)\cong\operatorname{Ext}^0_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathrm{NL}_{X/K},\mathcal O_X\otimes_K M).$$
Here $\mathcal O_X\otimes_KM$ denotes the sheafification of $U\mapsto\mathcal O_X(U)\otimes_KM$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. The first identification uses the trivial family as origin in the deformation torsor. These identifications preserve the usual square-zero deformation operations and the $K$-vector space operations: scalar multiplication by $a$ is pullback along the ring map $(b,m)\mapsto(b,am)$; addition is gluing two marked deformations over $\operatorname{Spec}K$ to the base $Y_M\amalg_{\operatorname{Spec}K}Y_M=Y_{M\oplus M}$ and then pulling back along $Y_M\to Y_{M\oplus M}$ induced by $(m_1,m_2)\mapsto m_1+m_2$. On automorphisms addition agrees with composition. The identifications are functorial under $K$-linear maps $M\to N$, acting by base change on the left and by the induced coefficient map on Ext on the right. No properness, dimension, or finite-presentation hypothesis on $X$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 0D17 (lemma-deform-spaces), split thickening Y=Spec K in Y_M; trivial origin and linear operations as in quot.tex Tag 0D1K (lemma-spaces-tangent-space), and artin.tex sections tangent-spaces and inf.

proof.text: Write $A_M=K\oplus M$ and $G_M=\mathcal O_X\otimes_K M$. The kernel $J_M=0\oplus M$ of $A_M\to K$ satisfies $J_M^2=0$, hence its conormal module is $J_M/J_M^2=M$. The pullback of this module to $X$ is $G_M$, since on a scheme chart the pullback is the sheafification of $\mathcal O_X(U)\otimes_K M$. Choose a basis $I$ of $M$. Tensoring the basis expansion identifies $G_M$ with the free module sheaf $\mathcal O_X^{(I)}$, so it is quasi-coherent even for infinite $I$. These are identities of sheaves, not an assertion that tensor commutes with arbitrary section functors.

source.place: Tag 0D17 (lemma-deform-spaces), conormal coefficient in the split case.

proof.text: Given a marked flat deformation $X'_M\to Y_M$, regard its special fibre as $X\hookrightarrow X'_M$. It is a first-order thickening because it is cut out by the square-zero ideal generated by $J_M$. The realization lemma identifies its etale site with $X_{\mathrm{et}}$. Apply the conormal flatness criterion to $(X\hookrightarrow X'_M)\to(\operatorname{Spec}K\hookrightarrow Y_M)$: the assumed flatness and Cartesian special fibre give the canonical isomorphism $G_M\xrightarrow{\sim}\ker(\mathcal O_{X'_M}\to\mathcal O_X)$. Restricting scalars along $K\to A_M$ therefore gives a square-zero extension of $K$-algebra sheaves with specified kernel $G_M$. An isomorphism of marked deformations respects this kernel identification, since its map on a generator $a\otimes m$ is determined by its map on $a$ modulo the ideal and its fixed image of $(0,m)$.

source.place: Tag 0D17 (lemma-deform-spaces), first exact diagram in the proof; spaces-more-morphisms.tex Tags 05ZS and 06BH.

proof.text: Conversely, start with $0\to G_M\xrightarrow{i}\mathcal A\xrightarrow{p}\mathcal O_X\to0$ of $K$-algebra sheaves with square-zero kernel. The realization lemma, with base $B=\operatorname{Spec}K$, realizes it as $X\hookrightarrow X'$. Define the base map on ring sheaves by $(b,m)\mapsto b\,1_{\mathcal A}+i(1\otimes m)$. This is multiplicative because the kernel is square zero. The morphism clause of the realization lemma gives $X'\to Y_M$. Locally choose a lift $\widetilde a$ of a section $a$ through the sheaf surjection $p$. Its conormal map sends $a\otimes m$ to $\widetilde a\,i(1\otimes m)=i(a\otimes m)$, hence is the prescribed isomorphism. The conormal criterion gives both flatness and the marked Cartesian special fibre. The same morphism clause identifies extension isomorphisms with marked deformation isomorphisms: maps fixing $K$ and $G_M$ fix every displayed image of $(b,m)$. The forward and reverse constructions recover each other's structure maps and kernel markings.

source.place: Tag 0D17 (lemma-deform-spaces), second exact diagram and realization; spaces-more-morphisms.tex Tags 05ZT, 05ZN and 06BH.

proof.text: Apply the sheaf-algebra extension classification to $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ and coefficient $G_M$. Steps 2 and 3 identify its extension isomorphism classes with $\operatorname{Def}_X(M)$, giving the displayed Ext-one bijection. The split extension $\mathcal O_X\oplus G_M$ has the base action of step 3 and is the structure sheaf of $X\times_KY_M$ on the common etale site (on a lifted chart it is $B\otimes_K A_M=B\oplus(B\otimes_KM)$). Its class is zero by the classification lemma. Thus this bijection uses the stipulated trivial origin, rather than an unspecified choice in a torsor.

For the split extension, a geometric automorphism over $Y_M$ reducing to the identity on $X$ fixes its kernel: $a\otimes m$ is the product of a lift of $a$ and the image of $(0,m)$, and changing the lift has zero product with the kernel. Conversely an extension automorphism fixes the base action $(b,m)\mapsto b+i(1\otimes m)$, so the realization lemma gives a unique geometric automorphism over $Y_M$. The extension classification identifies these automorphisms with $\operatorname{Ext}^0(\mathrm{NL}_{X/K},G_M)$. Explicitly they are $\alpha_d(a,g)=(a,g+d(a))$ for $K$-derivations $d:\mathcal O_X\to G_M$. Then $\alpha_d\alpha_e=\alpha_{d+e}$, so the contravariance of structure sheaves makes no difference to the asserted additive group identification.

source.place: Tag 08UG (lemma-huge-diagram-ringed-topoi), clause (2), and Tag 0D17, automorphism paragraph.

proof.text: Let $u:M\to N$ be $K$-linear and put $v=1\otimes u:G_M\to G_N$. On sheaf-algebra extensions its coefficient pushout is $P=(\mathcal A\oplus G_N)/\{(i(g),-v(g)):g\in G_M\}$, sheafifying this quotient; multiplication before quotient is $(a,h)(a',h')=(aa',p(a)h'+p(a')h)$. Its kernel is $G_N$ and its quotient is $\mathcal O_X$. This is exactly base change along $A_M\to A_N$: the mutually inverse ring maps are $a\otimes(b,n)\mapsto[(ba,p(a)\otimes n)]$ and $[(a,h)]\mapsto a\otimes1+\iota_N(h)$, where $\iota_N(c\otimes n)=\widetilde c\otimes(0,n)$. Lifts of $c$ are chosen locally through the sheaf surjection $p$; the formulas glue because the latter expression is independent of the lift: $(i(g)\otimes1)(1\otimes(0,n))=0$, because $i(g)$ is locally a sum of multiples of images of $(0,m)$ and $u(m)n=0$ in $A_N$. The balancing relations give precisely $(i(g),-v(g))=0$. These generator formulas commute with restriction, hence give the asserted sheaf identity and the geometric base change by the morphism clause of realization. The conormal map for $X\subset X_P$ over $\operatorname{Spec}K\subset Y_N$ sends $c\otimes n$ to $\widetilde c[(0,1\otimes n)]=[(0,c\otimes n)]$, the identity on $G_N$. Thus the conormal criterion applies with the original flat map $X\to\operatorname{Spec}K$ and proves flatness and the Cartesian special fibre.

source.place: Tag 0D17, split-base specialization; Tag 0GQ8 (remark-extensions-of-relative-ringed-topoi-functorial), coefficient pushout construction.

proof.text: By coefficient naturality in the extension classification, the pushout of step 6 has class $v_*[\mathcal A]$ in Ext one. The derivation automorphism $\alpha_d$ pushes out to $\alpha_{v\circ d}$, which is the same coefficient map on Ext zero. This proves the stated functoriality for all $u$, including noninjective maps and the zero map. Taking $u=a\,\mathrm{id}_M$ proves the scalar formula: the base ring map is exactly $(b,m)\mapsto(b,am)$ and the coefficient map is multiplication by $a$.

source.place: Tags 0GQ7 and 0GQ8, coefficient functoriality; artin.tex section-inf, scalar maps.

proof.text: For two deformations with sheaves $\mathcal A_1,\mathcal A_2$, their fibre product of rings $\mathcal F=\mathcal A_1\times_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal A_2$ is an extension by $G_M\oplus G_M=G_{M\oplus M}$. Its base action sends $(b,m_1,m_2)$ to $(b+i_1(1\otimes m_1),b+i_2(1\otimes m_2))$. Realization applies since its kernel $G_{M\oplus M}$ is quasi-coherent by step 1. The conormal map sends $c\otimes(m_1,m_2)$ to $(i_1(c\otimes m_1),i_2(c\otimes m_2))$, the prescribed kernel identification. The conormal criterion, with the original flat map $X\to\operatorname{Spec}K$, therefore proves flatness and the Cartesian special fibre over $Y_{M\oplus M}$. The two projections of ring sheaves give the two closed inclusions of the given deformations. This is their gluing along $X$: given compatible morphisms to a target $T$, let $g:X\to T$ be their common restriction. Their ring maps on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ combine uniquely to $g^{-1}\mathcal O_T\to\mathcal F$. Apply the morphism clause of realization with source thickening $X\subset X_{\mathcal F}$ and target the identity thickening $T\subset T$, over $K$. It gives the unique map $X_{\mathcal F}\to T$ with the specified restrictions. The identical calculation for the base is $A_M\times_K A_M=A_{M\oplus M}$; its spectrum is the asserted base pushout (a map to a scheme factors through an affine neighborhood of the common image of its sole point). Pulling back along the summation map of coefficient spaces is, by step 6, pushout of $\mathcal F$ along $G_M\oplus G_M\to G_M$, $(g_1,g_2)\mapsto g_1+g_2$.

source.place: Tag 0D17 via sheaf extensions; artin.tex section-inf, addition through the two-copy infinitesimal pushout.

proof.text: The construction in step 8 is exactly the Baer sum in the extension classification, hence corresponds to addition in Ext one. Together with step 7 and the zero class in step 4, this proves the vector-space assertion: all vector-space identities follow by applying the bijection to the corresponding identities in Ext. For automorphisms, step 5 gives composition as addition and step 7 gives the required scalar operations and naturality, so it gives the Ext-zero vector-space identification as well. All uses of geometric reconstruction required only quasi-coherence of $G_M$ (proved in step 1), and all uses of the conormal criterion required only the original flatness of $X/K$. No properness, finiteness of $M$, dimension bound, or finite-presentation hypothesis has entered.
